newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 70 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 70 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 50 billion bolivar ($105 million) auction of 177-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 14.35 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 10 billion bolivars ($21 million) in 267-day bills with a 14.61 percent coupon, and another 10 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 14.87 percent coupon.
Fifty billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are up from last week's 100 billion bolivar issue. Then 177-, 267- and 358-day notes carried 12.96, 13.17, and 13.38 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that firmed between 138 and 366 basis along the curve to 14.35, 18.43 and 19.65 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
